claim: Provisional G4 enforcing soak is RED and the enforcement worked: 7/7 nodes analyzed with 956 RSS samples, 4 nodes (024ca218,35904507,46482879,580ca257) show sustained-positive-trend process-RSS growth, and the scenario independently failed its ACTIVE wait (active=2/7 for 60 stalled attempts despite publishedActive=7/7, dominant witness readiness_inherited_active_gate_no_progress, with a hot defer loop spamming not-publications-write-leader reconcile decisions). Leaking nodes overlap the stalled ones, so the leak signal is plausibly the readiness hot loop accumulating; per the release epic this routes to an owner-level deterministic reproduction in the readiness/publication area before any further soak.

Two independent verifiers (rss-owner and soak-cutover aggregate rounds, 2026-08-25) flagged a pre-existing per-node coverage window: memory-leak-analyzer sets aggregate analyzed=analyzedNodeCount>0 and evaluateMemoryLeakAssertions checks only the aggregate, so a soak where one node analyzes clean and six are under-sampled passes the runtime gate, and a node emitting zero samples never appears in nodes[]. The G4/G5 release-side soak evaluation MUST therefore enforce per-node coverage itself from the report (every configured node present, analyzed:true, >=30 samples, no insufficient-* reason) before reading a soak PASS as leak-freedom.

GCP soak run release-0-2-memory-soak-2026-08-25T04-52-00Z FAIL root-caused by independent investigation: multi-host addressing/port-blocks validated end-to-end (every probe hit the correct host:port; mesh formed; publication PUBLISHED epoch 4); the failure was a genuine formation stall under fully-committed CPU (nodesPerHost=4 on e2-standard-8, cpus 2.0/node + heap profiling) - four joiners never completed the join runtime composition (admin WS binds last), with join retry churn, membership reconcile deferred against a cache_stale_watermark repair-deferred write-leader, and a zero-backoff ~500Hz message-router reconnect loop on refused peers. The 2026-08-21 movielens GCP run (1 node/VM) formed cleanly, so the soak config was changed to vmCount 7 x e2-standard-4, nodesPerHost 1. Secondary harness defect: multi-host failure log collection queries only host0's daemon (test/distributed/run-runtime-helpers.js:577-582 -> collectContainerFallback), silently losing non-primary hosts' node logs - fix required before diagnosing any future multi-host red.

Second GCP soak attempt (release-0-2-memory-soak-2026-08-25T05-40-00Z, 7x e2-standard-4, 1 node/VM) failed startup readiness at ~331s with a DIFFERENT dominant reason than attempt 1: priority_recovery_actuation_state_action_required - four system partitions (schema_operations, sql_transactions, sql_transaction_participants, sql_write_operations) stuck eligible_but_no_operation_created/needs_operation with owner rebalancer-leader, blocking boundary operation_scheduling, wait mode event_driven, next action create_recovery_operation never actuated; active gate stalled 2/7 with snapshot coverage flapping. Full 7-node logs captured (multi-host log-collection fix b4b06a5bb verified working). The identical 7-node soak formed and ran on the local dev box on 2026-08-22, so the class appears GCP-latency-exposed; related sealed quest blocked-spread-evaluation-event-wake covers the flat-timer non-wake shape. G4 provisional soak evidence will be collected with the epic's sealed local command; the GCP-exposed formation stall stays tracked for the latent-blocker census, out of the 0.2 sealed claims.

First fully-executed enforcing soak (release-0-2-memory-soak-local-2026-08-25T06-12-00Z, sealed local command, 31.6min): the G4 enforcement machinery is VALIDATED end-to-end - all 7 nodes analyzed:true on process_rss_bytes, 930 samples (>=129/node, min 30 satisfied), per-node reasons present, failOnDetection fired. Two product signals: (1) verdict BLOCK_PERFORMANCE_INVALID with dominantReason=nodeAdmissionBlocked - load admission stayed blocked under sustained control-plane readiness pressure for the whole window, the CL-044 class at 7 nodes; (2) leakDetected on node 6b9bc8aa: sustained-positive-trend, +195MB (+32.9%) over the 25min analysis window at 7.85MB/min slope (15x the 524KB/min threshold), positiveDeltaRatio 0.82, peak 790MB, no recovery - plausibly recovery-churn accumulation on a node spinning in the blocked-readiness loop, to be re-measured after the CL-044 fix lands; if a clean-admission soak still shows it, it becomes its own leak quest. Per the sealed G4 rule the red routes to the owner-level deterministic path (CL-044 quest formation-barrier-spread-cure-liveness), not another soak. RSS series preserved at test-output/reports/.playback/release-0-2-memory-soak-local-2026-08-25T06-12-00Z/sustained-write-throughput/samples.ndjson (141 samples for the leaking node); heap snapshots correctly not captured (790MB never neared the 2g limit trigger).

claim: Post-CL-044 enforcing GCP G4 is valid RED on exact committed HEAD cdda789003b2 / source bbd70acf45475c8b: 7/7 one-node-per-VM nodes analyzed, 1,068 valid process-RSS samples, no coverage warnings, and node a7990536 has sustained-positive-trend RSS growth +41,402,368 bytes (+9.83%) at 1,516,705 bytes/min, positiveDeltaRatio 0.773, tail slope 1,500,808 bytes/min, no recovery. The load scenario formed and ran 30 minutes, then failed only the required memory assertion; total GCP cost was /bin/bash.6638 and all VMs were torn down.
rulesOut: CL-044 formation/admission repair alone is sufficient to certify leak freedom; per-node aggregate coverage or the prior readiness-blocked local sample explained away the RSS trend.

claim: Systemic post-CL-044 memory discrimination: the enforcing GCP G4 RED is not a repeat of the prior admission-blocked local measurement. Load ran for 30 minutes with 7/7 process-RSS coverage and 1068 valid samples, yet node a7990536-1a35-4e54-8503-aa67f41f3cef crossed the leak predicate (+41,402,368 bytes, +9.834%, 1,516,705 bytes/min, positive-delta ratio 0.7727). The node changed across the two RED runs, but the common role is replica_operations-p1 leadership: the prior local leaking node led that partition among 43 leaders; in GCP a799 took that leadership after 4 snapshots and retained it for the remaining 313 while owning no other partition leader. GCP retained only 25 operation IDs and 189,665 bytes of final steps_history; after warmup its V8 heap/external/ArrayBuffer endpoints fell while RSS rose, although the late RSS maximum coincided with a late V8 heap-capacity maximum. This narrows the next falsifier to ledger-owner allocation churn/high-water retention versus true native retention; it does not yet prove a permanently retained object.
rulesOut: Rules out CL-044 alone being sufficient for the 0.2 memory gate, a 7/7 coverage gap, node identity, total leadership count, generic reconnect/log churn, and a simple endpoint-retained JS heap or external-buffer leak. Do not weaken the RSS floor or rerun another soak before an owner-level deterministic discriminator.

claim: Whole-plane correction to the single-node leak label: every one of the seven post-warmup GCP processes grew RSS, by 22.07, 32.91, 39.48, 39.71, 47.27, 62.60, and 166.16 MiB. Six escaped the final leak boolean only because their positive-delta ratio was below 0.70; their tail RSS slopes were still 0.76-2.18 MiB/min, all above the configured 0.5 MiB/min slope ceiling. Across nodes, V8 heap-used peaks rose 34.79-215.50 MiB above post-warmup starts and heap-total peaks rose 35.86-180.39 MiB, while external-memory endpoint deltas stayed within +/-0.88 MiB. Therefore a799's replica_operations-p1 leadership remains a useful role discriminator for monotonicity but cannot own the whole symptom. The release blocker is cluster-wide V8 allocation/heap-capacity high-water with no demonstrated recovery plateau, plus at least one exact unbounded diagnostics owner found in readiness planning (buildOwnerKeys and buildsByToken); the current boolean under-reports the breadth but its RED verdict is valid.
rulesOut: Rules out treating the six non-flagged nodes as memory-clean, a single ledger-leader-only leak theory, external/ArrayBuffer retention as the dominant whole-plane mechanism, and weakening the positive-delta threshold to obtain green. The deterministic path must bound retained owner state and prove recovery/plateau before another GCP soak.

Candidate SHA-256 a7c83190349ca29efc88b605323c8ebc49a0a777340c849971ec117791d57f37; ordered path-content manifest SHA-256 49937a83fbf704d6310d2e0a48728a1574286e5abcf69060d25b57ce991b6066. The verifier confirmed the fail-honest 513-reconcile red-on-revert, bounded 256 readiness samples and 32 queue samples, exact aggregate/drop counters, shutdown graph release, no parallel runtime authority, direct and coupled-tail green proof, static guards, and safe local thermals.

Separate lifecycle-retention follow-on: readiness completed-snapshot, build-option, and deferred-snapshot memo maps retain removed-node owner keys until process shutdown. Preserve it as an explicit residual owner-lifecycle boundary; do not silently fold an unproven eviction policy into the current stable-membership measurement.

Exact-source GCP soak ceacbf64ba4e4c46 passed the sealed memory contract: 7/7 nodes analyzed, 1011 process-RSS samples, 102-119 post-warmup samples per node, no insufficient-analysis reason, and leakDetected false. The bounded diagnostic owners removed the prior catastrophic outlier, but all seven full-window and tail RSS slopes remain positive and no node reports recovery, so this is not evidence of literal whole-plane plateau; removed-node membership-churn retention remains a separate follow-on owner.
